notes: Line 1 is NOT ICAO-conformant: it reads PE<ARGGONZALEZ<<SARA<EMMA, placing a filler at position 3 and ARG at 4-6, so the name field is shifted one character right. A strict parse yields issuing state "<AR" and surname "GGONZALEZ" -- that is correct behaviour, not a bug. Recorded here as PE/ARG, which is what the VIZ prints.

Blank template specimen: every VIZ field and the whole MRZ are literally X (X<XXXXXXXXXXXXXX<<XXXX<XXXXX). Belongs to the robustness set, not the accuracy set -- it must yield no field values rather than garbage ones.

TRC is Terra Condifea, the fictional issuing state Cetis prints on its sample passports. Deliberately absent from crates/mrz/src/countries.rs -- a real document can never carry it, so UnrecognizedIssuingCountry firing here is correct.

BDR is the Bundesdruckerei specimen-printer code, not an issuing state. It is deliberately absent from crates/mrz/src/countries.rs so a BDR document cannot pass as a real German D<< passport; UnrecognizedIssuingCountry firing here is correct. year.kind is expiry: issued 24.09.2008, expires 24.09.2018.

D<< is Germany's real MRZ code: a single letter padded with fillers. Exercises the repair-gate defect where country_name() is called on the untrimmed 3-byte slice, so country_name("D<<") is None and the dropped-filler repair is discarded.

The MRZ is physically redacted on the source image, so there is no document number to expect and it cannot be a positive corpus entry. The old CORPUS array carried the placeholder string REDACTED-NO-GROUND-TRUTH-MRZ here, which was never a real value.

PO is a genuine letter O in both the MRZ and the VIZ, not the P0/P< filler form. The homoglyph is the trap this manifest exists to remove from filenames. VIZ prints the given name as 'MYONG SUN'; the MRZ concatenates it to MYONGSUN.

Replaced 2026-09-02. The image previously under this name was a back side carrying an MRZ, and read IC/MCO with valid checksums -- reported at the time as a Tier-1 false positive, which it was not: that is what a correct Monaco identity-card read looks like. The author renamed the back side to Monaco_ID_Specimen_XXXX_back_mrz.png and supplied the real front here. Kept as a note because the mistake shaped the harness: a negative control is only as good as its no_mrz tag.

Known Tier-1 miss since 2026-08-17: reproducibly returns 'no MRZ found' against the current OCR/parser. Kept as a corpus entry with its known document number so the hit rate counts it -- dropping it would inflate the rate by shrinking the denominator.
